comparison: Perfect agreement on cell cycle defects (C47-C53). Both evaluations support the S-phase accumulation findings from flow cytometry. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation while peer review explicitly acknowledges the flow cytometry results without critique.

Perfect agreement on cytokinesis findings (C7, C54, C57-C61). Both evaluations support the role of Mtss2/Abba in cytokinesis using live imaging and cultured cells. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance while peer review explicitly states authors 'found Abba played a prominent role in cytokinesis.'

Perfect agreement on Nedd9 knockdown phenocopy (C71-C74). Both evaluations support that Nedd9 knockdown partially mimics Mtss2 knockdown effects. OpenEval notes the distinction in PH3 effects while peer review acknowledges 'similar results' without concerns.

Perfect agreement on RhoA regulation (C9, C75-C79, C108). Both evaluations support the RhoA signaling mechanism. OpenEval details FRET-based measurements with statistics while peer review implicitly accepts these findings as part of the 'compelling evidence' for signaling partner interactions.

Perfect agreement on clinical genetic evidence (C11, C80-C86). Both evaluations support the link between MTSS2 mutations and human microcephaly. OpenEval emphasizes de novo nature and conservation while peer review explicitly acknowledges 'compelling evidence' for clinical relevance.

Strong agreement on protein-protein interactions (C8, C63, C66, C68-C69). Both evaluations support Y2H and co-IP findings showing Mtss2-Nedd9 interaction. OpenEval emphasizes orthogonal methods while peer review explicitly notes the interaction studies and localization findings without criticism. Peer review additionally references C107.

Strong agreement on patient mutation phenotype (C12, C90-C95, C101). Both evaluations support that the human variant causes distinct phenotypes from knockdown. OpenEval interprets this as gain-of-function/dominant-negative while peer review explicitly acknowledges the 'disorganized radial glial fibers' and lack of cell division impact. Peer review additionally references C96-C97.

Agreement on computational predictions (C87-C89). Both evaluations support the bioinformatic evidence for mutation pathogenicity. OpenEval notes limitations of computational predictions but finds convergent evidence sufficient; peer review implicitly accepts these analyses without explicit discussion.

Strong agreement on radial glial morphology and knockdown effects (C4-C6, C34-C36, C38, C40-C41). Both evaluations support the core phenotypic observations. OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation across multiple approaches while peer review provides 'compelling evidence' statement. Peer review additionally covers C37, C42-C43, and C98 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on morphological observations (C134-C135). Both evaluations support these findings though with some uncertainty. OpenEval notes the interpretation regarding direct neuronal role remains uncertain; peer review implicitly accepts these as additional supporting data without explicit discussion. OpenEval additionally references C132 and C137.

Agreement on experimental validation (C34). OpenEval evaluates tool validation including sequence homology (C32-C33) and knockdown efficiency; peer review implicitly accepts the shRNA knockdown approach without questioning efficiency. Both support the technical foundation.

Partial overlap on mutation mechanism speculation (C96-C97). OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable speculation but lack of direct gain-of-function experiments. Peer review acknowledges the distinct phenotype (C90-C95, C101) which informs the mechanistic speculation but doesn't explicitly evaluate the gain-of-function hypothesis. OpenEval covers broader mechanistic speculation (C123-C129) not addressed by peer review.

Minimal overlap on summary statements (C98). OpenEval evaluates comprehensive summary claims (C98-C100, C138-C140) as supported by the full dataset. Peer review references C98 as part of the broader evaluation of Mtss2's role but focuses on specific experimental findings rather than summary statements.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic speculation about PI(4,5)P2 binding and membrane-cytoskeleton linkage (C106, C117, C121, C133) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are plausible hypotheses requiring direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic hypotheses.
